panel.settings.title: Settings
panel.settings.autostartWarning: Autostart will break if Keyji.exe is moved or deleted
catalog.title: Add language
catalog.empty: All available languages are already in your set
catalog.footnote: Keyji doesn't download languages itself — “download” opens Windows Settings, where you install the language manually
confirm.title: Install language
confirm.body:
The language “{0}” isn't installed in Windows yet. Keyji will open Settings and copy the name to the clipboard.

Then, in Settings:
1.  Click “Add a language”
2.  Paste the name into the search box  (Ctrl+V)
3.  Select the language and install it
welcome.title: Welcome to Keyji
welcome.intro: Keyji lives in the tray next to the clock and helps you switch keyboard layouts and input languages. Here's how to use it:
welcome.gesture.right.text: Right-click the tray icon to open the panel — languages, pinning, settings, and exit.
welcome.gesture.left.text: Left-click the icon to turn the pinned language on or off.
welcome.location.title: Don't move Keyji
welcome.location.text: Keep Keyji.exe in a permanent folder. Moving or deleting the file breaks autostart and you won't be able to launch Keyji again — don't leave it in Downloads or a temporary folder.
welcome.footer: You can close this window — Keyji keeps running in the tray.
firstrun.permanent.title: Permanent languages
firstrun.permanent.hint: Keyji never turns these layouts off — they're your base languages. Uncheck one if you'd like Keyji to manage it (enable/disable).
